scalars.scalar_value: Experience providing senior-level administrative support in a complex educational, arts, nonprofit, or similarly multifaceted environment.

Any combination of training and experience which would provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be equivalent to completion of the twelfth (12th) grade supplemented by college-level coursework AND five (5) years of increasingly responsible and varied administrative support experience.

items.item_text: Any combination of training and experience which would provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be equivalent to completion of the twelfth (12th) grade supplemented by college-level coursework AND five (5) years of increasingly responsible and varied administrative support experience.
Experience providing senior-level administrative support in a complex educational, arts, nonprofit, or similarly multifaceted environment.
Experience supporting multiple departments, programs, faculty, and staff while managing competing priorities and deadlines.
Experience coordinating the operational needs of specialized instructional, laboratory, studio, production, performance, or event spaces.
Experience providing professional, public-facing customer service and responding effectively to questions, concerns, and complaints.
Experience supporting events, performances, exhibitions, or other public programs.
Experience with ticketing, registration, reservation, point-of-sale, or similar customer-management systems.
Experience preparing reports, reconciling transactions, handling deposits, and maintaining accurate financial records.

A District on-line application on http://hr.fhda.edu/careers/. *In the application, you will provide information, which demonstrates your understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff. Additionally, you will be asked to explain how your life experiences, studies or work have influenced your commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion.
A current resume of all work experience, formal education and training.
Modern office management practices, procedures, technology, and computer equipment and applications, including word processing, database, and spreadsheet applications.
Perform advanced and complex administrative and program support work accurately, within established deadlines, and with use of independent judgment.
Demonstrated proficiency using office technology, databases, spreadsheets, scheduling systems, and other administrative software.
Organizational practices as applied to the analysis, evaluation, development, and implementation of programs, policies, and procedures within assigned areas of responsibility.
Understand the organization and operation of the District and of outside agencies as necessary to assume assigned responsibilities.
A cover letter addressing your qualifications for the position.
Principles and techniques of conducting analytical studies, evaluating alternatives, making sound recommendations, and preparing and presenting effective and technical reports.
Coordinate and oversee assigned administrative, budgeting, and fiscal reporting activities.
Applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, regulations, ordinances, and District policies and procedures relevant to assigned area of responsibility.
Plan, organize, and carry out assignments from management staff with minimal direction.
Record keeping and filing systems and methods.
Analyze, interpret, summarize, and present administrative and technical information and data in an effective manner.
Basic statistics, business arithmetic, and bookkeeping.
Evaluate and develop improvements in operations, procedures, policies, or methods.
Business letter writing and the standard format for reports and correspondence.
Research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery methods, procedures, and techniques.
English usage, grammar, spelling, vocabulary, and punctuation.
Interpret, apply, and explain applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, regulations, ordinances, and District policies and procedures relevant to assigned area of responsibility.
Prepare, review, and present reports and other correspondence and communications in a clear and concise manner.
Maintain accurate databases, records, and files.
Maintain confidentiality and be discreet in handling and processing confidential information and data.
Perform arithmetic, financial, and statistical computations accurately.
Organize and prioritize a variety of projects and multiple tasks in an effective and timely manner; organize own work, set priorities, and meet critical time deadlines.
Effectively use and keep current with computer systems, software, and modern business equipment to perform a variety of work tasks.
Use tact, initiative, prudence, and independent judgment within general policy, procedural, and legal guidelines.
Establish, maintain, and foster positive and effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.

Techniques for providing a high level of customer service by effectively dealing with the public, students, and District staff, including individuals of diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation.

Demonstrate understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff.
